title: Wilson's theorem split at the half: (p-1)! congruent to m! times ((-1)^m times m!), over the constructed integers
statement: For a modulus p = 2m+1 satisfying this kernel's PrimeCond, `Int.factorial m` times ((-1)^m times `Int.factorial m`) is congruent to -1 modulo p. This is Wilson's theorem with the product (p-1)! cut at m and its upper half reversed, and it holds for BOTH parities of m. Nothing here is imported or axiomatised; `Kernel::axiom_footprint` for this declaration is EMPTY. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. It does not by itself say anything about quadratic residues: the residue reading is the even-m specialisation, which is F:int-firstsupplementarylawresidue. The sign is the entire content -- the unsigned form, (m!)^2 congruent to -1 for all m, is FALSE (at m = 3, p = 7 the two sides are 1 and 6). Primality is load-bearing and is not discharged.

formal.statement: theorem Int.wilsonHalfSplit : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : And (AxNat.le (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))) (((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat.dvd x1 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat x1 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (Eq.{1} AxNat x1 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))))))) -> Int.ModEq (Int.ofNat (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))) (Int.mul (Int.factorial x0) (Int.mul (Int.pow (Int.neg Int.one) x0) (Int.factorial x0))) (Int.neg Int.one)))

provenance.source: Derived mechanically from the unfiltered emit of `cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection`, which prints one TSV row per declaration whose fields are (prelude, kind, display name, axiom-footprint size, direct type declarations, direct declarations, direct theorems, Kernel::render_lean(declaration.ty())). formal.statement is that last field verbatim; depends_on is the direct-theorem column intersected with this ledger's registered facts; axiom_footprint is the footprint-size column, cross-checked by the whole-prelude nat_axiom_inventory run recorded in the second evidence row. No field was hand-transcribed and no prose was authored. `title`, `statement` and `notes` were then REPLACED by hand (lane first-supplementary-residue, ADR-1235); every other field is the generator's output unmodified.

notes: Route (`int_prelude/first_supplementary_residue.rs`, ADR-1235), four steps, every one of which already existed except the reflection's two permutation predicates: `Int.prodRange_split` at (a,b) = (m,m) cuts `Int.factorial (p-1)` -- `sub (succ (mul 2 m)) 1` iota-reduces to `mul 2 m`, and `two_mul_eq_add_self` carries that to `add m m` -- ; `Int.prodRange_permute` at the reflection k -> `sub (pred m) k` reverses the upper half; `Int.modEq_prodRange_lt` makes each reversed factor congruent to (-1)*(k+1); and `Int.prodRange_scaledIndexEqPowMulFactorial` at a := -1 collapses that to (-1)^m * m! in one step. `Int.wilson` closes it. THE POINTWISE CONGRUENCE needs, in Nat and for k < m, succ k + succ (m + ((m-1)-k)) = succ (2m). `Nat.add` recurses on its RIGHT argument, so `add x (succ y)` iota-reduces and exactly ONE `succ_add` is needed; the rest is add_comm/add_assoc, `Nat.sub_add_cancel` (which turns ((m-1)-k) + k into pred m) and `Nat.succ_pred_of_pos`. 0 < m is never a hypothesis -- it is derived from k < m wherever it is needed, so the m = 0 boundary is excluded by primality alone (p would be 1). LIFTING TO Z NEEDED NO ofNat_add LEMMA: `Int.add (ofNat a) (ofNat b)` is definitionally `ofNat (add a b)`, so `nat_eq_to_int` carries the whole identity across; `Int.modulus_modEq_zero` then gives p congruent to 0 mod p unconditionally and `Int.modEq_add_left_cancel` peels the shared ofNat (k+1) off both sides. TWO DEFECTS, both found by a throwaway probe that inferred every intermediate against a FREE m in one run rather than by bisecting: `Nat.sub_sub_self` was declared before the `Nat.add_sub_cancel_left` it consumes (UnknownConst across all 297 nat_prelude tests, naming neither lemma), and `Nat.succ_pred_of_pos` states `m = succ (pred m)`, not the reverse -- one `d.symm`, presenting as a bare TypeMismatch at the whole prelude build. The numeric content is re-runnable: `python3 docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1235-first-supplementary-residue-checks.py` (rows C5 through C8).
